result.title: Beyond Robust Algorithmic Recourse: Sharing the Burden of Validity through Model Multiplicity
result.summary: Algorithmic recourse provides actionable recommendations that enable individuals to achieve favourable outcomes. Implementing recourse for individuals requires significant time and effort, thus emphasizing robust recourse: recommendations that remain valid even under future model updates. While robustness preserves validity, we show it introduces systematic harms by constraining feasible recommendations to regions that disproportionately reflect majority behavior, reducing individual flexibility and amplifying disparities. Thus, non-robust recourse risks invalidation, whereas robust recourse creates a preference for high-density regions in the data that induces unfairness. However, this trade-off is driven by an implicit assumption that individuals alone should bear the burden of validity. We challenge this narrative and show that strategic model selection can help maintain validity while relaxing robustness requirements for individuals. By leveraging multiplicity, the existence of equally good yet competing models, system owners can share this burden with individuals, thus resolving the tension between validity and unfairness.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究算法追索（algorithmic recourse）中稳健性与公平性的冲突，提出通过模型多重性（model multiplicity）让系统方与个体分担有效性负担，从而在放松稳健性要求的同时维持推荐有效。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文关注表格决策场景下个体追索推荐的公平性与模型更新，不涉及视觉或多模态推理中的内部状态、证据获取或生成机制；「模型多重性」与多 latent 假设仅为词面相似，缺少可核查的具体方法线索，故排除。
